title: Q1 2026 Perf baseline notes (WIP)
body:
Doc purpose
- Scratchpad for perf baseline + representative workload suite. Not a spec; this is where we capture early results, variance suspects, and open questions before freezing the Q1 2026 baseline.
- Audience: runtime, kernels, SRE/obs, Applied ML/evals.

Current state (as of 2026-02-12)
- Harness: run-manifest schema + validator merged (benchmark-lab#21432). Workload generators: chat streaming (benchmark-lab#21455), long-context prefill (benchmark-lab#21471), embeddings high-QPS (benchmark-lab#21488).
- Runtime instrumentation: scheduler queue/batch assembly metrics in (redwood#21503). Kernel selection debug dump in (redwood#21519) behind perf-run flag.
- Perf-canary wiring: representative suite nightly + gating mode in progress (perf-canary#21562) — still tuning thresholds/noise model.
- Decision pending: baseline freeze build/tag (see Slack eng-runtime/1764107317). Proposed anchor: runtime build from release branch cut week of 2026-02-10 (exact tag TBD once CI is green across regions).

Measurement boundaries (notes from Slack eng-runtime/1763261084)
- TTFT definition (tentative): server-received request timestamp -> first token available to stream on the wire (server side). We exclude client read/SDK buffering.
- TPOT definition (tentative): per-output-token time for tokens 2..N measured server-side; reported as mean + percentiles across requests (separately from TTFT).
- Throughput: tokens/sec for generation workloads; req/sec for embeddings; always paired with concurrency + batch stats.
- IMPORTANT: We need to pin exact boundaries in the manifest and dashboards so TTFT isn’t accidentally “first-token rendered by client.”

Workload taxonomy candidates (v1 suite)
A) Chat streaming (short prompts, variable decode)
- Why: dominant production cohort; sensitive to scheduler fairness + continuous batching.
- Shape:
  - Prompt (prefill) bins: 32–128 tokens (60%), 129–512 (35%), 513–1k (5%)
  - Decode bins: 64–192 tokens (55%), 193–512 (35%), 513–1k (10%)
  - Concurrency: stepped ramp 8 -> 16 -> 32 -> 64 (hold 5 min each) per model/GPU
  - Streaming pacing: server push; client reads fast (avoid backpressure from client)
- Metrics to highlight: TTFT p50/p95/p99; TPOT p50/p95/p99; tokens/sec; scheduler queue wait p95/p99; batch size distribution.

B) Long-context summarization / prefill stress (large prefill, modest decode)
- Why: exposes prefill/decode overlap, KV cache pressure, backpressure thresholds.
- Shape:
  - Prefill target: 8k–16k tokens (mix), decode: 256–512 tokens
  - Concurrency: 1 -> 2 -> 4 -> 8 (this saturates quickly; higher conc becomes “overload behavior” test)
  - Warm vs cold cache: run both (see caching decision below)
- Metrics: TTFT (main), prefill latency breakdown, queue wait, GPU utilization/saturation indicators, load shed/drop counters.

C) Tool/function calling (bursty multi-turn)
- Why: production has bursty short turns + intermittent longer turns; tests queueing discipline and fairness under burst.
- Shape (proposed):
  - Session model: 3–6 turns, 1–2 tool calls in 40% of sessions
  - Turns alternate: short user prompt + short assistant, then tool call result (small), then assistant continuation
  - Burst model: 30s burst / 90s steady cycles
- Status: not implemented in harness yet (candidate for v1.1 if we can’t stabilize by freeze).

D) Embeddings high-QPS (small payload)
- Why: throughput-first SKU economics; catches CPU/network overhead regressions + batching inefficiencies.
- Shape:
  - Input sizes: 16–64 tokens (70%), 65–256 (25%), 257–512 (5%)
  - Concurrency: constant high QPS driver (target 2k–10k req/min depending on SKU)
- Metrics: req/sec, p50/p95/p99 latency, CPU usage on gateway, batching stats.

Baseline run matrix (draft)
- Regions: us-east, eu-west (must). Optional later: us-west, ap-southeast.
- Hardware SKUs: H100 (must), A100 (must), L40S (where models supported + capacity).
- Models (top deployed families):
  - Llama family: 8B/70B class (exact variants pinned in manifest; avoid swapping minor revisions mid-baseline)
  - Qwen family: 7B/14B class
  - Mistral family: 7B class (and MoE variant if it’s in top traffic)
- NOTE: Model list is not final here; we should sync with Jonas Weber on “top deployed” from telemetry snapshot date.

Caching in baseline: decision + action items
- From Slack eng-runtime/1764196509: we will report BOTH cold and warm scenarios.
  - Cold: cache disabled or cache flushed between runs (document method).
  - Warm: fixed prefix cache enabled + KV cache reuse where applicable; workload seed ensures repeatable prefixes.
- Open question: what’s the least hacky way to do “cold” without lying to ourselves?
  - Option 1: unique prompts each request (but then you’re changing token distribution / entropy).
  - Option 2: explicit cache flush endpoint per run segment.
  - Option 3: restart worker between segments (too expensive + adds warmup noise).
- TODO: choose and document in run-manifest (Claire + Omar).

Initial run results (VERY PRELIMINARY; do not quote outside eng)
- These are from early sweeps used to validate harness + instrumentation, not the final baseline. Sample sizes are still small in some cells; variance is not fully modeled.

1) Chat streaming workload (streaming on, cold cache)
- Model: Llama-family 8B-class (pinned build in manifest)
- Concurrency: 32 steady (post ramp)
- us-east / H100 (single node pool)
  - TTFT: p50 ~ 180–220 ms, p95 ~ 420–520 ms, p99 ~ 650–850 ms
  - TPOT: p50 ~ 14–18 ms/token, p95 ~ 22–30 ms/token
  - Tokens/sec: ~ 2.5k–3.4k tok/s (dependent on decode mix)
  - Observations:
    - Queue wait p99 spikes correlate with batch assembly time outliers (likely backpressure setting + batch cap).
    - Kernel selection is stable (no unexpected fallbacks).
- eu-west / H100
  - TTFT: p50 ~ +10–25 ms vs us-east, but tails sometimes +100–150 ms when host contention present (suspect placement).

2) Long-context prefill workload (cold cache)
- Model: Llama-family 70B-class
- Prefill 16k-ish / decode 256
- us-east / H100
  - TTFT: p50 ~ 1.8–2.4 s, p95 ~ 3.2–4.4 s, p99 ~ 5.0–6.8 s
  - Biggest tail drivers seen in traces:
    - Queue wait due to large request admission during bursts.
    - Occasional kernel fallback event (see below) causing cliff.
- NOTE: redwood#21541 claims p99 TTFT improvements on long-prefill by tuning backpressure thresholds; we need to re-run with a clean A/B on the same fleet configuration.

3) Embeddings high-QPS
- Model: embedding model vX (pinned)
- us-east / L40S
  - Throughput: 1.2k–2.0k req/s at p95 latency ~ 18–35 ms (depends heavily on client driver settings)
  - Variance note: CPU saturation on driver hosts becomes the bottleneck before GPU in some runs; need to standardize driver instance type.

Kernel fallback / selection issues (known)
- L40S: observed unexpected fallback on some long-context regimes (sequence length boundary). Symptom: step-function increase in TTFT and drop in tokens/sec.
  - We believe this is kernel auto-selection choosing a conservative kernel due to misclassified seq length regime.
  - Mitigation for baseline: pin kernel for affected cells (temporary) OR restrict baseline seq lens to avoid boundary.
  - Owners: Yuki Sato + Hiro Tanaka.
  - Action: add “kernel debug dump” to all baseline runs (sampled is ok but baseline should be 100% recorded for attribution).

Variance / noise suspects (collating from SRE thread eng-sre/1763512044 + scratch experiments)
1) GPU clocks / power management
- Clocks not locked -> 5–15% tokens/sec drift across runs.
- Ask: can we standardize clock locking on benchmark fleet? (Sean)

2) Placement / noisy neighbors
- In eu-west we’ve seen TTFT tail spikes with the same config; correlates with node-level CPU steal and NIC interrupts.
- Proposed: dedicated benchmark nodes or strict taints; at minimum, record node id + co-tenancy hints in manifest.

3) Warmup procedure
- Without warmup, first 2–5 minutes show drift (JIT/kernels, cache priming).
- benchmark-lab#21471 added standardized warmup for long-context; need analogous warmup for chat streaming + embeddings.
- TODO: decide warmup duration and what “counts” as warmup (discard samples? separate phase?).

4) Client/driver bottlenecks
- For streaming workloads, client read speed can become limiting if using a naive Python loop.
- We should prefer a high-perf driver and measure server-side timestamps only.
- TODO: confirm SDK/harness uses server-side metrics emitted by runtime, not client observed.

5) Batch/caching config drift
- Small changes in defaults (max batch size, queue timeout, prefix cache toggle) can look like regressions if configs aren’t pinned.
- Must include full scheduler + batching config in manifest (ENG-4822 acceptance).

Workload representativeness checks (Applied ML / Evals)
- Jonas + Maya asked us to ensure the suite mirrors production cohorts without leaking prompt content.
- We’re using token-length histograms + synthetic prompts; still need to validate:
  - Do we match production decode length distribution for chat streaming?
  - Are we under-representing “short prefill + long decode” cases (creative writing) that stress decode scheduling?
  - Do tool-calling patterns matter for batch assembly (bursty turns) enough to include in v1?
- TODO: schedule 30 min review with Applied ML on the current bins/weights (use telemetry snapshot date in notes).

Open questions (need decisions before freeze)
1) Baseline sample size
- What’s the minimum N per cell (model x sku x region x workload x cache-mode) to reliably detect a 5% regression at p95/p99?
- Sana to propose noise model + sample size guidance. Tie to perf gating thresholds.

2) Regression thresholds
- Do we gate on absolute TTFT/TPOT deltas, relative deltas, or both?
- How do we treat improvements that shift cost/throughput tradeoffs (e.g., lower p99 TTFT but -5% tokens/sec)?
- Suggested: define primary + secondary metrics per workload with “allowed tradeoff envelope.” Needs signoff from Mateo + Neha.

3) Overload behavior
- Should baseline include an overload segment (beyond saturation) to ensure graceful degradation and no meltdown?
- If yes, what’s pass/fail? (no crash, bounded queue, load shed counters within policy).

4) Cross-region comparability
- If eu-west hardware/driver versions lag, do we block baseline freeze? Or treat regions separately with explicit env capture?
- Leaning: allow separate baselines but require manifests to make drift explicit.

5) Cold vs warm cache protocol
- As above: need an explicit method that’s reproducible and not too expensive.

TODOs (next 2 weeks)
- [Rina] Lock down run naming conventions: {date}.{region}.{sku}.{model}.{workload}.{cache}.{runtime_tag}.{scheduler_profile}.{seed}
- [Claire] Write “baseline freeze checklist” (min sample sizes met, manifests complete, kernel dumps present, warmup protocol, dashboards linked).
- [Sofia] Confirm scheduler profile(s) we will freeze for baseline (one default + one high-throughput profile?) and document guardrails.
- [Hiro/Yuki] Resolve kernel fallback boundary or provide pinning guidance + document in kernel selection matrix.
- [Sean/Aisha] Confirm benchmark fleet isolation steps and what gets enforced vs only recorded.
- [Allison/Sergio] Dashboard draft: panels for TTFT/TPOT p50/p95/p99 + variance view + links to manifest/traces.
- [Connor/Sahana] Perf-canary gating mode: decide PR vs nightly coverage and exception process.
- [Jonas] Provide telemetry-derived weights for request mix; validate bins.

Risks
- Capacity: benchmark fleet contention will slow baseline sweep; we need reserved windows (see Neha email approval thread referenced in project list).
- Variance: without clock locking + isolation, p99 comparisons are noisy; risk of over-gating and blocking releases.
- Scope creep: tool/function calling workload may push freeze date; we may need to ship v1 without it and add v1.1.

Notes to self / random observations
- When queue timeout is low, TTFT p95 looks great but drop/load-shed counters spike under burst (not acceptable unless explicitly in overload segment).
- For long-context, batching can harm TTFT tails if we wait too long to assemble (prefill is expensive; fairness vs batch efficiency needs explicit policy).
- Make sure manifests record: driver/CUDA version, NCCL version, GPU clocks state, NUMA affinity, container image digest.

Next meetings
- Weekly baseline sync (runtime + SRE + Applied ML): Thu 11:00 PT
- Kernel selection deep dive: Tue 14:00 PT (Hiro/Yuki + Rina)
- Threshold/noise model review: Wed 10:00 PT (Sana + Claire + Connor)

Changelog
- 2026-02-12: Added preliminary long-context numbers; added kernel fallback notes for L40S; updated TODO list.
- 2026-02-03: Added caching decision notes (cold+warm) and updated workload bins for chat streaming.
- 2026-01-21: First insertion of chat streaming early sweep results; added variance suspects from SRE thread.
- 2025-12-18: Created doc; initial taxonomy outline + links.
